title: Soft Wake Flow: incremental weight streaming and KV handover for predictable startup latency
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleet customers require throughput guarantees immediately after scaling events. Current cold-start exhibits long tails: median time-to-first-token ~150ms for hot replicas, but cold nodes show 95th percentile time-to-first-token > 2.5s and time-to-full-residency (all model shards + KV primed) often > 30s under tenant-heavy workloads. This hurts bursty workloads and violates SLOs for dedicated commitments.

Proposal: Implement a Soft Wake Flow that combines incremental weight streaming (priority-first shard streaming with progressive execution readiness) and KV handover (selective KV prefix snapshot transfer and shadow prefetch) to reduce client-observed cold start without requiring full weight residency. Key ideas: incremental streaming pipeline that makes early layers available first so short-context requests can be served sooner; shard prioritization based on typical request depth profiles; limited KV handover from existing warm replicas to new nodes for hot prefixes using a secure delta-snapshot protocol; admission control to limit concurrent wakeups to prevent overload; metered network throttling to keep burst bandwidth within fleet budget.

Goals and success metrics: reduce 95th pct time-to-first-token on cold starts from >2.5s to <800ms for typical tenant profiles; reduce time-to-full-residency by 30%; maintain throughput guarantees during ramp (95% of reserved throughput available within startup window); keep additional network cost under +12% for typical workloads.

Design decisions and trade-offs: incremental streaming increases short-lived network IO and complexity in kernel readiness management but significantly shortens tail latency; KV handover trades cross-node snapshot traffic for lower KV cache miss rates on new nodes. We avoid full model snapshot replication to reduce storage and transfer duplication. The admission control policy favors tenants with reserved throughput commitments (Dedicated SLA) during mass recovery. Private deployments will keep handover optional and restricted to internal VPC ranges for security compliance.

Implementation Phases:
1) Prototype incremental weight streamer and priority shard selector (canary runtime flag).
2) Implement KV delta-snapshot transfer (secure, attestable stream).
3) Admission controller and bandwidth metering hooks + canary rollout orchestration.
4) Observability: new telemetry for time-to-first-token, shard-readiness events, KV handover success/failure, and network bytes per startup.

Rollout plan: small canary (5 nodes) in dedicated fleet -> collect metrics for 48h -> expand to 20% fleet -> monitor target tenant SLOs -> full rollout with automatic rollback on threshold breach.

Notes on compatibility: must integrate with existing weight residency manager and preexisting KV cache priming API. Work includes runtime changes and a control-plane flag to toggle handover per customer.

Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SoftWakeFlow-Design
Load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rtc/warm-pool-soft-wake?orgId=1
acceptance_criteria: New incremental streamer can serve first-token for short (<128 tokens) requests on cold node within 800ms in 95% of test runs under standard tenant mix
KV handover reduces KV miss rate on new node by >=40% for top-100 prefixes during first 60s after attach
Admission control prevents >3 concurrent startup streams per host by default; override allowed per customer via config
Telemetry available for time-to-first-token, shard readiness timestamps, KV handover bandwidth per startup, and rollout health summaries
Automated canary rollout with configurable thresholds and automatic rollback on SLO breach
tasks: Design priority shard ordering heuristics and implement selector in residency manager
Extend runtime to support layered readiness and early execution on partial shards
Build KV delta-snapshot exporter and secure transfer API
Add admission controller hooks in orchestrator and expose customer-level policies
Create load tests that emulate tenant burst patterns and measure TTF token and throughput during ramp
Instrument telemetry and add Grafana panels and alerts for regressions

2026-03-04 - Luca Moretti: Prototype incremental streamer started. Early microbenchmarks show 1.9x reduction in time-to-first-token for tiny contexts on single-node simulation.
2026-03-06 - PM review (Jon Reed): Please ensure admission controller respects Dedicated SLA ordering; flagged as dependency for rollout gating.

2026-03-08 - Security (Marta Liu): KV handover must be restricted to VPC-only flows for Private customers; we will add attestable transfer tokens. Marked security_review_required=true for private deployments.
2026-03-10 - Infra (PR feedback): Network metering needs to emit per-startup metrics for chargeback; opened follow-up ENG-834502 to add accounting hooks.

2026-03-12 - Design update: choose shard-first ordering: embedding + first self-attention blocks -> middle -> final blocks. Rationale: short-context inference often only needs early layers; verified in sample inference traces.
2026-03-13 - QA: created load harness and initial canary test plan. Observing KV handover failures when primary node is pinned; need retry/backoff logic.
